newsitem.title: FRANCE: Axor plans bigger aircraft on Liege-CDG route.
newsitem.headline: Axor plans bigger aircraft on Liege-CDG route.

text.p: Intra-European express company, Axor, a subsidiary of French group, Jet Services, said it was planning to put a bigger aircraft on its nightly Liege-Paris CDG all-cargo service.

"We currently operate a two-tonne capacity Metroliner on the route and are likely to change to a five-tonne Fokker 27 in the near future as a result of the buoyant level of traffic," a Jet Services official told Reuters.
At the beginning of 1997, Axor replaced a Metroliner on its nigthly Kassel (Germany)-CDG route with an F27, the official said.
Axor had no immediate plans to replace the Shorts SD330 freighter aircraft it operates on a nightly route between Coventry and CDG, the official added.

Jet Services, via its airline subsidiary, Air Jet operates domestic all-cargo flights linking Paris with Marseille, Montpellier, Toulouse, Strasbourg and Rennes, using its fleet of three BAe 146QC (quick change) aircraft. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+ 5017
